content: 1. Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome in patients under 16 years old: Use cimetidine only if the benefits outweigh the risks. The recommended dosage is 20-40 mg/kg/day, administered either intravenously (IV) or orally (PO), divided every 6 hours. 2. Neonates (less than 28 days old): The dosage is 5-20 mg/kg/day, administered IV or PO, divided every 8-12 hours. 3. Infants: The dosage is 10-20 mg/kg/day, administered IV or PO, divided every 6-12 hours. 4. Elderly patients: Cimetidine is not the drug of choice due to an increased risk of confusion and potential drug interactions. 5. Cimetidine and dofetilide: Cimetidine increases dofetilide levels by reducing renal clearance. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 6. Cimetidine and eliglustat: Cimetidine increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. If co-administered with strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily in extensive and intermediate metabolizers. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are used alongside strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 7. Cimetidine and fezolinetant: Cimetidine increases fezolinetant levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors increases fezolinetant AUC and peak plasma concentration. 8. Cimetidine and lomitapide: Cimetidine increases lomitapide levels significantly by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Cimetidine and pimozide: Cimetidine increases pimozide levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 10. Cimetidine and alosetron: Cimetidine increases alosetron levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Cimetidine and alprazolam: Cimetidine increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Cimetidine and artemether/lumefantrine: Cimetidine increases artemether/lumefantrine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Cimetidine and atazanavir: Cimetidine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces atazanavir solubility. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, for treatment-naïve patients, take atazanavir simultaneously with the H2-receptor antagonist or at least 10 hours afterward. Adjust dosage for treatment-experienced patients as per recommendations. 17. Cimetidine and atorvastatin: Cimetidine increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Cimetidine and axitinib: Cimetidine increases axitinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely and reduce the dose if necessary. 19. Cimetidine and bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens: Cimetidine increases the effects of this combination by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Cimetidine and belladonna/opium: Cimetidine increases the effects of belladonna and opium by reducing their metabolism.
